profiles.field_rule: Research trial: Narrow silver-white lanceolate panicle with numerous short hairy rames on a long rachis. The head overlaps the silver-bluestem group: verify a 9–20 cm panicle, robust cauline stems, green shiny acute sessile spikelets (3–4.5 mm) and 9–14 mm awns against B. laguroides subsp. torreyana; no local voucher or glume measurement is established by the current reference image.

profiles.field_rule: Research trial: Diffuse, broad open Eragrostis panicle on a perennial tuft, with a hair-fringed inner ligule per Hill Country and Kew GrassBase. The most meaningful discriminator is the sticky, viscid panicle axis and branch bases: the current photographs have not demonstrated stickiness, so no species-level confirmation is possible. Keep awn state unscored; compare nonglandular and glandular lovegrasses with mature spikelets.

profiles.field_rule: Research trial: Tufted fringed windmillgrass with about 2–5(7) distinct digitately placed, short one-sided flowering branches and conspicuously hairy lemmas. FNA under Chloris ciliata gives fertile lemma hairs about 0.5–1.5 mm and awns only 0.9–1.4 mm. The ligule can be absent or a tiny ciliate remnant, so this trial deliberately leaves both ligule and awn choices unknown instead of falsely excluding ambiguous collars and small awns.

profiles.field_rule: Research trial: Early wildrye forms an erect true spike, commonly with two outward-spreading spikelets at most rachis nodes; the long awns are on real glumes and lemmas, not hairs. The three source-labeled pictures alone cannot distinguish hybrids or confirm an independent Hays plant.

profiles.field_rule: Research trial: Broad loose open fall-panicum panicle on geniculate or spreading green stems, with no long lemma awns. A tiny ciliate membrane may appear as a hair ring; both inner-ligule answers are accepted rather than treating one photographic interpretation as a hard conflict. Do not code bent stems as stolons: FNA reports rooting at lower nodes especially when in water, but this is not proof of a true runner. Compare actual glume proportions and pedicel arrangement with witchgrass and other Panicum.

profiles.field_rule: Research trial: Tiny often matted hardgrass with heavily overlapping leaves and a short crowded racemose head that may partly remain inside the upper sheath. profiles.field_rule: Research trial: Tufted Paraguayan windmillgrass bearing 2–9 digitate/subdigitate racemes that may curve downward. Unlike tiny ciliate or absent-ligule S. ciliata, FNA under Chloris canterae reports a short erose membranous ligule. Distinguish with the comparatively longer 3–14 cm racemes, longer 1.5–3 mm fertile-lemma hairs and 2.4–5.5 mm lemma awns, not the shared finger-like outline. Leave awn choice unscored: this Lab has no precise 2–6 mm short-awn option.

profiles.field_rule: Research trial: Robust blue panicgrass with an open to somewhat contracted panicle and knotted short rhizomes, not simply an airy annual roadside Panicum. The stem nodes are commonly swollen and can be hairy; these NODE hairs are NOT the true ligule. A short ligule may have a ciliate margin, so either hairs or a tiny membrane can be a reasonable first-look category. Compare mature 2.4–3.4 mm spikelets, rhizomes and florets with Panicum dichotomiflorum before proposing a Hays occurrence; forage planting remains unresolved.
